messages:
Jess: FYI customer AcmeChat reporting sudden 502/5xxs from hosted inference endpoint /v1/generate, started ~10:02 UTC. They pasted a request_id: req_0a7b9c3d and a short repro curl. They say most requests fail with 'upstream error (502)'.

Jess: Repro curl they used:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-13b\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```

Jess: Customer timeline: 10:01 first success, 10:02 spike to 30% 502s, 10:05 80% 502s. They sent response headers: x-request-id=req_0a7b9c3d, x-region=us-west-2.

Mike: @Jess thanks. Can you paste the gateway logs + control-plane error? Also tag @Oncall SRE. Suspect control-plane dependency failing (auth/session or routing).

SupportBot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 5xx for /v1/generate (us-west-2). Error class: control-plane:dependency_failure. 5xx rate = 42% (5m).

Linda: Pasting snippet from control-plane router logs around req_0a7b9c3d:
```
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z ERROR routing-policy-fetch failed: context deadline exceeded (timeout 1.2s) route_id=acmechat
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z WARN auth/session lookup failed: redis dial tcp 10.0.12.8:6379: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:03:13Z ERROR proxy upstream write failed: net/http: request canceled (client disconnected) req=req_0a7b9c3d
```

Linda: Looks like dual symptoms: routing policy fetch timeouts and auth/session store errors. Config DB (routing policy) timeouts frequently cause 502s because control-plane can't compute routing decisions.

Arnav: Confirmed from infra metrics: config-db (pg-primary-usw2) CPU and connection count spiked at 10:02. There are a bunch of long-running queries from rollout-service and policy-sync. Replica lag is 120s. Connection pool for control-plane (pgx) is exhausted -> timeouts.

Arnav: Immediate mitigations I can do: scale config-db read pool, bump control-plane PG connection pool limit, or flip routing service to use cached policy file. Which do we prefer for minimal blast radius?

Mike: Priority: reduce customer impact ASAP. Options ranked: 1) enable routing cache fallback (no db fetch) for control-plane (fast). 2) Temporarily scale DB replicas. 3) Throttle policy-sync jobs to reduce load.

Jess: How do we toggle routing cache? do we have an internal endpoint?

Linda: There is an admin toggle: POST /admin/controlplane/route-cache/fallback with body {"enable":true}. Only available from control-plane-admin network. I'll run it and report. @Arnav can you watch DB while I toggle?

Arnav: watching. If routing cache fallback doesn't cut it, I'll scale the pg read replicas x2 and restart the long-running policy-sync pods.

Linda: Executing toggle now...
```
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer admin-svc\" \
  https://controlplane-admin.internal/_admin/controlplane/route-cache/fallback \
  -d '{"enable":true}'
```

Linda: Response: 200 OK, fallback=enabled. Rolling config push to all control-plane pods.

Oncall SRE: Noted. I'm running the runbook: restart policy-sync job and check session store (redis) health.

SupportBot: Update: 5xx rate fell from 42% -> 8% within 60s of fallback enable. Still seeing auth/session errors intermittently.

Jess: Customer just posted: error rate reduced, but still seeing some 502s for longer inputs. They provided new request id req_0a7b9c3e.

Linda: Looking at logs for req_0a7b9c3e: auth/session lookup returned error -> fallback to anonymous session incorrectly triggered a check that failed. We need to increase redis client socket timeout and confirm failover logic in auth service.

Arnav: Scaling pg replicas now (increase from 2 -> 4). Also bumping connection_pool_max for control-plane from 80 -> 160 via config rollout. This will take ~30s to roll.

Arnav: Also restarted the long-running policy-sync job (k8s job policy-sync-2026-0315). That should reduce DB pressure in next 2 minutes.

Mike: Good. Also can we reduce rate of new incoming requests to hosted inference in us-west-2 temporarily (traffic shaping) while we stabilize? We can shift some routing to us-east-1. Ops-team has a GA routing policy to shift 10-30% traffic cross-region.

Jess: Customer accepted temporary rate shift to mitigate. Please note they're on paid dedicated flow but hosted model.

SupportBot: 10:07: 5xx rate now 2.1% in us-west-2. Replica lag falling to 10s. Redis latency back to normal.

Linda: Post-action notes for incident: root cause appears to be a combination of: a) config-db experiencing high connections from policy-sync/rollout jobs, b) control-plane connection pool limits too low causing timeouts, c) redis (session store) transient network blips causing auth lookups to fail. These combined to cause a control-plane dependency cascade and 502s for inbound requests.

Mike: Next steps: create INC ticket, notify customer with summary & workaround (routing-cache enabled, temporary cross-region shift). Schedule follow-ups: increase control-plane connection_pool_max permanently, introduce circuit-breaker for config-db calls, hard-rate-limit policy-sync jobs and add DB slow-query analysis.

Jess: I'll write the customer update and include repro steps and mitigation. Also attaching customer provided curl + request_ids.

Arnav: I'll create a PR with two config changes: pool_max bump and graceful backoff with exponential retries for routing-policy fetch (with local cache fallback). Also schedule a DB maintenance window to move heavy jobs off peak hours.

Linda: Adding to SRE backlog: add an alert that watches combined symptoms (pg connection exhaustion + redis latency) to trigger preemptive mitigation.

Mike: Thanks team. Recommended postmortem owners: Linda (control-plane), Arnav (infra), Jess (customer comms). I'll file the incident INC-2026-042 and assign.

Jess: Customer update posted: \"we observed a control-plane dependency issue causing higher error rates between 10:02-10:08 UTC. Temporary measures applied (routing cache + cross-region routing). Our SREs are investigating and we'll follow up with a timeline for permanent fixes.\"

SupportBot: Incident INC-2026-042 created and linked to this thread.

Jess: Closing loop with customer: they confirmed traffic looks stable and no further 502s for last 6 minutes. I'll keep the ticket open until postmortem completed.

Mike: Solid. After postmortem, let's roll the permanent pool increase and the circuit-breaker change behind a feature flag and test in staging.

Linda: Will add playbook entry for \"routing-cache fallback\" to the control-plane runbook and document when to use it.

Arnav: Also raising an ops-cost note: policy-sync should use paged queries and respect DB connection budget. I'll follow up with the rollout-service owners.

Jess: Thanks all. Marking as resolved for customer, keeping incident open for internal follow-up. :white_check_mark:
